chosen.chosen: The exact text of every output: the 'Would move / Would not move', 'Moved / Did not move' and 'Put back / Did not put back' lists, each as 'name -> Folder/' or 'name : reason', ending with the next command to run, and the error lines starting 'organize-downloads:'.
chosen.why: The builder builds each scene from the UX alone and the README shows one run, so the words the user sees are fixed here; a list per outcome ending with the next command lets the user decide the next run from the output alone.

chosen.chosen: The plain run also lists the files it would not move with why, clashes included, and --move does exactly what the plain run listed.
chosen.why: The user decides to move from the plain run's list (KR1.4); a clash shown only after the move would be a surprise.

chosen.chosen: A file's extension is the part after the last dot, other than a leading dot; so backup.tar.gz goes to Archives and .DS_Store or README are of no type and listed as not moved.
chosen.why: The decided types name single extensions; without this rule builders would treat .tar.gz and dotfiles differently.

chosen.chosen: Folders directly in Downloads, the type folders included, and what they hold are left as they are; only files directly in it are sorted.
chosen.why: AC2 speaks of each file directly in Downloads; moving folders or re-sorting type folders would move what the user did not ask for.

chosen.chosen: A file or other non-folder already named like a type folder (such as a file named Images) makes each file of that type not moved, with the reason 'Images exists and is not a folder'.
chosen.why: The tool deletes and overwrites nothing, so it cannot make the folder; telling why keeps every file accounted for (KR1.5).

chosen.chosen: Undo works per sorted folder; a file not put back stays in the last move so a later --undo tries it again; the last move ends when every file of it is put back or another --move moves files; an undo leaves empty type folders in place; with nothing to undo it says so and exits 0.
chosen.why: Lets the user clear a clash and retry without losing the way back, while an undo still removes and overwrites nothing (AC9).

chosen.chosen: Errors: both --move and --undo, an unknown option, more than one folder, or a folder that does not exist or cannot be read stop the run with a one-line reason, a pointer to --help, exit status 1 and no change; a run that went through every file exits 0, files not moved or not put back included.
chosen.why: The CCS decided only the --move with --undo case; the same treatment for every misuse keeps one rule, and exit 0 for a finished run keeps not-moved files (normal) apart from errors.

chosen.chosen: organize-downloads --help prints a usage line, what the tool does, the three options and the six types with their extensions, changes nothing and exits 0.
chosen.why: Common practice for a command-line tool; the errors point to it, and the user can see the agreed types from the tool itself.

chosen.chosen: Lists are in order of file names, with paths relative to the sorted folder named in full on the first line.
chosen.why: A stable order lets the user compare the plain run with the move, and the full path on top shows which folder (such as ~/ダウンロード) was sorted.

chosen.chosen: Key results in the order: files lost or changed, files not put back by undo, files not sorted into their type folder, plain-run list differing from the move, files left without a reason.
chosen.why: Losing a file costs more than any time saved; a move that cannot be undone keeps the user from sorting at all; only then do sorting, preview and telling bring the user closer to G1.

chosen.chosen: Box kinds in the figures written as Mermaid entity codes (#lt;person#gt;) so the angle brackets render.
chosen.why: A bare <person> in a Mermaid label is read as an HTML tag and dropped when rendered.

chosen.chosen: A file that cannot be moved or put back for a reason other than a clash, such as no permission, is left as it is and named with the system's reason, and the run goes on with the other files.
chosen.why: Stopping halfway would leave some files moved and others not with no list of either; going on and naming each keeps every file accounted for (KR1.5) and leaves the moved ones for --undo.

chosen.chosen: Each command printed for the next run names the sorted folder last where the user named one.
chosen.why: Otherwise copying the printed command would act on ~/Downloads instead of the folder the user named.

chosen.chosen: Where nothing moves or is put back, the first line is 'Nothing to move / Nothing was moved / Nothing was put back in <folder>.', followed by the list of files left with why.
chosen.why: Keeps the rule that the first line names the sorted folder in full, and still names every file left.

chosen.chosen: KR1.5 counts, per run, the files the run is about: run plainly or told to move, every file directly in the sorted folder not listed as moved or to be moved; told to undo, every file of the last move not put back; files in the type folders not of the last move, and folders, are not counted.
chosen.why: Those are the files the user expects a word on from that run; files the run never touches would make the count grow with no fault of the run.
